A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable text, equations, seven figures, two algorithms, and Appendices A–D. Matching these materials reveals no gaps that prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original TinyStories-8M sampling experiments, ARI and log-probability distribution estimates, error analyses, and comparisons across prompts.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Sections 4–6 and Appendices C–D, including Figures 2–7.

M1.justification: Annealed transition path sampling, exponential biasing, MBAR reconstruction, and Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged. The expanded distinction between target and biasing observables already appeared in v1 Appendix C.4 and introduces no new implemented component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TinyStories-8M using ARI and completion log-probability, with the same principal prompt, training-data reference distributions, and four additional validation prompts in Appendix D.

E2.justification: Direct/ancestral sampling remains the evaluated comparator in the main experiments and Appendix D. Newly cited distribution-sharpening methods appear only in related work; calling direct sampling state-of-the-art changes positioning, not comparator membership.

E3.justification: Both retain temperature-1 decoding, 100-token completions, the ARI cap of 15, sampling budgets, annealing schedules, 10% burn-in, and exclusion at Gelman–Rubin values of at least 1.1. Appendix D's prompt selection and sampling settings also match.

E4.justification: The chain-length/error analysis in Figure 4, repetition case study in Figure 5, overlap diagnostic in Figure 6, and prompt comparison in Figure 7 are retained. Section 6 expands the motivation for the existing case study without adding analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Both report 100 bootstrap replicas, nominal 96% confidence intervals, Wilson intervals for direct sampling, and the same convergence reporting. v2 removes duplicated bootstrap-description text without changing the statistical procedure or reported run information.

E6.justification: Figures 2–7 retain identical plotted results, including trajectories, density estimates, uncertainty curves, overlap matrices, and prompt comparisons. The repetitive completion example and associated findings also match; no result entries or numerical values are added or revised.

T1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 expand intermediate algebra for the existing importance-sampling and MBAR identities, yielding the same partition-function equations. These are equivalent mathematical restatements. Appendix B–C mathematics is unchanged apart from equation numbering.

C1.justification: The abstract and five listed contributions remain unchanged. Section 7 strengthens applicability claims by explicitly dismissing small-model scope as a limitation and asserting that the approach can operate through APIs without access to model weights.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds a specific rationale for early filtering through repetition proxies: accurate ARI evaluation requires completed, multi-sentence text. Section 7 adds discussion of API access and log-probability requirements for alternative proposals. Existing interpretations of repetition and appendix limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a supplementary-code repository reference and states that a minimal implementation is provided. This supplies access information absent from v1; the repository's contents are not established by the PDFs. Existing pseudocode, settings, and implementation guidance remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Karan and Du (2025), Ji et al. (2026), and Garrahan (2016), connecting distribution sharpening to TPS and Doob transforms. It also newly asserts that direct sampling is the only directly comparable method for this setup.

P1.justification: The introduction replaces its four-part outline with a three-stage roadmap and foregrounds existing observable-selection guidance. Local rewrites expand the MBAR explanation, filtering motivation, and conclusion, alongside grammar and duplication fixes. Section order and overall organization remain intact.

P2.justification: All seven figures retain their artwork, axes, legends, and results. Limited presentation changes include spelling corrections in Figures 2–3 captions, expanded equation displays, and reflow of text and figure placement; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 improves readability through clearer workflow framing and MBAR exposition, explains the practical motivation for the retained case study, and adds a supplementary-code pointer. These provide limited gains in usability and reproducibility documentation. Stronger claims about large-model and API applicability receive no new validation, limiting the evidential benefit of those additions.
